The study titled Efficacy of Circumcision Devices in Tanzanian Males: Guiding Circumcision Device Design and Supply Forecasting, published in The Journal of Urology in 2013 (Volume 190, Issue 2, Pages 544-550), focuses on the evaluation of circumcision devices specifically for Tanzanian males. The research provides insights into the design and supply chain requirements for these devices, aiming to optimize their use in public health interventions. 2. The Global Harmonization Task Force Study Group 2 released a document in 2000 titled Medical Devices Post-Market Surveillance: Global Guidance for Adverse Reporting for Medical Devices. This guidance outlines standardized procedures for monitoring and reporting adverse events associated with medical devices, ensuring safety and efficacy in their post-market phase. 3. The World Health Organization (WHO) published a report in 2012 titled Use of Devices for Adult Male Circumcision in Public Health HIV Prevention Programmes: Conclusions of the Technical Advisory Group on Innovations in Male Circumcision. This document, developed in Geneva, Switzerland, provides recommendations on the implementation of circumcision devices as part of HIV prevention strategies, emphasizing their role in public health programs.
